summary:
The **back cover** of *Deep Learning with Python, Third Edition* (Chollet and Watson).

The blurb says deep learning has changed the world twice in less than a decade: first when Python libraries such as Keras, TensorFlow and PyTorch moved neural networks from lab experiments to production systems, and again through large language models and other generative AI tools. The third edition is described as a **complete rewrite** with new chapters on Transformers, building your own GPT-like LLM, and generating images with diffusion models.

**What's Inside:** hands-on, code-first learning; coverage from basics to generative AI; intuitive math explanations; examples in **Keras, PyTorch, JAX and TensorFlow**. The audience is readers with intermediate Python skills; no previous machine learning or linear algebra experience is required.

Author bios: François Chollet is co-founder of Ndea and creator of Keras; Matthew Watson is a software engineer at Google working on Gemini and a core maintainer of Keras. Endorsement quotes come from Anthony Goldbloom (founder of Kaggle), Santiago Valdarrama (ml.school), Aran Komatsuzaki (EleutherAI) and Salvatore Sanfilippo (creator of Redis). Print book owners get the digital formats free at manning.com/freebook.
